# soulsensis

> Your soul knows best. Listen to your soul. All it has wanted is to be heard. A book that's been crafted from someone's actual journal, lived experiences. Built over 5 years of writing. It's real. It's grounded. Written by a human. Published anonymously as soulsensis. The book: Your soul knows best (Sit still enough to hear it).

## The book

- [Your soul knows best](https://soulsensis.com/book.html): essays on comparison, wanting, the shadow, blame, attention, surrender and contentment. Not self-help steps; one person thinking honestly from inside their own life.
- The book is being finished as one larger book, with the author's journals added, so the page count and contents may change.

## A conversation

- [A conversation](https://soulsensis.com/conversation/): 60 minutes, one to one, by voice. A$120, or 4 sessions for A$440, valid 6 months. Booking opens soon; email hello@soulsensis.com until then.

## Topics (the book's chapters)

- [Chapter 1: A fraction of who I am](https://soulsensis.com/essays.html#chapter-1): Comparison, living by someone else's script, and the wanting and waiting that keep you small.
- [Chapter 2: Behind lucid eyes](https://soulsensis.com/essays.html#chapter-2): Facing what hurts instead of hiding it: dark thoughts, the shadow, friendships that end, and seasons that pass.
- [Chapter 3: Water the grass in front of you](https://soulsensis.com/essays.html#chapter-3): Dropping blame, framing events as neutral, choosing where attention goes, and seeing that identity can change fast.
- [Chapter 4: The cost of fighting yourself](https://soulsensis.com/essays.html#chapter-4): The addiction to stress and resistance, and why becoming yourself is the simplest and the most demanding thing.
- [Chapter 5: Sit still enough to hear it](https://soulsensis.com/essays.html#chapter-5): No longer trying to shine, stepping aside from wanting, and coming home to the quiet voice underneath.
- [Chapter 6: Contentment, the only destination](https://soulsensis.com/essays.html#chapter-6): Living it: presence, meaning found by acting in the world, and a soul that was never broken.

## Essays

- [Half alive, half dead](https://soulsensis.com/essays/half-alive-half-dead/): There's a state a lot of people live in without ever naming it. You're not really living, but you're not dying either. You're half alive and half dead. The question it answers: What does it mean to be half alive and half dead? It's living without really living, and without dying either: a life you can't authentically call your own, swayed by everyone around you. No one is here to tell you how to live. You decide who you are, and then you live it.
- [Where are you rushing to?](https://soulsensis.com/essays/where-are-you-rushing-to/): Everyone feels rushed, but no one is asking: where are you rushing to? I think one of the most important things in life is to be able to slow down. Our… The question it answers: Why do I always feel rushed? Acceleration only gets you to a place faster. It does not mean you are happier, it just means you will have another goal sooner. Before you pick up your phone tomorrow morning, ask yourself where you're rushing to, and if you can't answer, slow down until you can.
- [You get who you are](https://soulsensis.com/essays/you-get-who-you-are/): By making your own imprint onto this world by way of output and giving and creative endeavours, the world you help create is richer with your… The question it answers: Why do I never get what I want? Wanting implies lack of having, so we never get what we want. We get who we are. Adopt the state you want first, and give from the truth of your heart rather than on the condition that you receive.
- [Perception is key](https://soulsensis.com/essays/perception-is-key/): Like most people, I scrolled through LinkedIn and Instagram and felt the dread wash over me.
- [We weren't meant to be living the way we do](https://soulsensis.com/essays/we-weren-t-meant-to-be-living-the-way-we-do/): We weren't meant to be living the way we do. Most of us feel it. And most of us feel we don't have a choice.
- [You do not get what you want](https://soulsensis.com/essays/you-do-not-get-what-you-want/): There are mornings I wake under a weight I can't name and can't shake. It sits underneath everything, telling me something in my life is off. And… The question it answers: Why do I feel stuck in life? This wanting is what traps you, and forcing change doesn't work. The more you grip to wanting, the further the object of your wanting moves away from you.
- [The receptiveness I was waiting for](https://soulsensis.com/essays/the-receptiveness-i-was-waiting-for/): There is a particular kind of tiredness that lives at the edge of a life that has not yet committed to itself. It is not the tiredness of the body. It is… The question it answers: How do I stop waiting for the right moment? The conditions are never right. The moment is the only moment. And the person who has to arrive is the one already standing here.
- [Born to be fearless](https://soulsensis.com/essays/born-to-be-fearless/): We were born to be fearless, to pursue the greatest things that are available to us, to pursue what is most meaningful to us. Yet we all know there are a… The question it answers: How do I find my purpose in life? The thing that you come here to do is actually not linked to what you think makes you money.
- [The utility of pain](https://soulsensis.com/essays/the-utility-of-pain/): I don't know why I have such a dark perspective behind my lucid eyes. The question it answers: How do I let go of pain I keep holding on to? If it has already given you what it had to give, you are allowed to put it down.
- [Transparency and integration of the shadow](https://soulsensis.com/essays/transparency-and-integration-of-the-shadow/): I remember bracing myself for an attack that never came.
- [The past was great](https://soulsensis.com/essays/the-past-was-great/): I used to say it all the time: those were the best years. I said it like a fact. And for the rest of that day, nothing in front of me stood a chance.
- [Here for a season](https://soulsensis.com/essays/here-for-a-season/): A friend once told me that some people you meet in life are here for a season only. I never expected it to apply to the friend who said it. Once I…
- [Seasons come and go](https://soulsensis.com/essays/seasons-come-and-go/): You may be screaming into your pillow in agony and frustration. That's okay. Sometimes it's necessary.
- [Gratitude is underrated](https://soulsensis.com/essays/gratitude-is-underrated/): Gratitude is underrated as fuck. Perhaps modern society has rendered it “wishy-washy”, a bit cringe, but on application to your life, you notice insane… The question it answers: How does gratitude change your life? Gratitude is a feeling that comes from where you put your attention, so you can practise it on purpose, even when something looks like a loss. When I find the spark of gratitude in a bad moment, I can see which thoughts the feeling came from and change them. Keep doing that and you get a deep relaxation, and you stop attracting the same problems.
- [Blame and responsibility](https://soulsensis.com/essays/blame-and-responsibility/): Self-blame is destruction dressed as accountability. The difference between self-blame and responsibility is radical. One dismantles you. The other…
- [Framing](https://soulsensis.com/essays/framing/): We label a job loss as "bad" before we have even left the building. The word arrives that fast, and once it is there, we stop looking at what is actually…
- [The currency of attention](https://soulsensis.com/essays/the-currency-of-attention/): The grass is not greener on the other side. It is greener where you water it, and attention is the water: your awareness, your deliberate thinking, poured…
- [Your identity is a lot more malleable than you think](https://soulsensis.com/essays/your-identity-is-a-lot-more-malleable-than-you-think/): Most of what you call "who I am" is a habit of thinking you have repeated long enough to mistake for a fact.
- [Swift and revolutionary change](https://soulsensis.com/essays/swift-and-revolutionary-change/): We are taught to trust slow change. Slow and steady, one small habit at a time. But some changes don't ask permission to go slowly.
- [The simplest things](https://soulsensis.com/essays/the-simplest-things/): The simplest things are the most complex things to do. I learned that in the dark stretch, when I could not see a way out.
- [The lighthouse does not try to shine](https://soulsensis.com/essays/the-lighthouse-does-not-try-to-shine/): For years I had more ideas than I could write down and not the nerve to put a single one into the world. I called it not being ready yet. It was something…
- [The step aside](https://soulsensis.com/essays/the-step-aside/): Nobody teaches you to step aside. Not your parents, not your school. You are taught to push, to chase, to accumulate.
- [Listen to your soul](https://soulsensis.com/essays/listen-to-your-soul/): Do you realise that your inner state strongly dictates your external environment? Why do some people who are brought up with nothing achieve millions?… The question it answers: How do I listen to my intuition? So, listen, deeply, your soul's nudges. Those quiet intuitive callings are 10x more powerful than what the mind can conceive.
- [Step away](https://soulsensis.com/essays/step-away/): You need to be kind to yourself. Kindness to yourself is a very important skill set, and it requires you to understand that even if you might be doing… The question it answers: How do I stop a habit I know is hurting me? So the only way you can truly get rid of any vice that you know is not good for you is if you simply just stop resisting.
- [The walk: the alignment](https://soulsensis.com/essays/the-walk-the-alignment/): Somewhere between one tree and the next, something opens.
- [Navel gazing: the spiritual trap that kills meaning](https://soulsensis.com/essays/navel-gazing-the-spiritual-trap-that-kills-meaning/): There is a difference between reality and actuality. Reality is how your life looks from the inside. Actuality is what is happening.
- [The actuality of the soul](https://soulsensis.com/essays/the-actuality-of-the-soul/): Much of what I read in self-development, spirituality and metaphysics rests on one quiet assumption: that something is fundamentally wrong with you. That…

## Questions

- [Why do I feel like I'm just existing?](https://soulsensis.com/question/just-existing-not-living/): You're living a life you can't authentically call your own. You struggle to look at yourself in the mirror.
- [Why do I always feel rushed?](https://soulsensis.com/question/why-do-i-always-feel-rushed/): Acceleration only gets you to a place faster. It does not mean you are happier. It just means you will have another goal sooner.
- [How do I find my purpose in life?](https://soulsensis.com/question/how-do-i-find-my-purpose/): The thing that you come here to do is actually not linked to what you think makes you money.
- [How do I listen to my intuition?](https://soulsensis.com/question/how-do-i-listen-to-my-intuition/): So, listen, deeply, your soul's nudges. Those quiet intuitive callings are 10x more powerful than what the mind can conceive.
- [How do I stop a habit I know is hurting me?](https://soulsensis.com/question/how-do-i-stop-a-habit-hurting-me/): So the only way you can truly get rid of any vice that you know is not good for you is if you simply just stop resisting.
- [How do I stop waiting for the right moment?](https://soulsensis.com/question/how-do-i-stop-waiting-for-the-right-moment/): The conditions are never right. The moment is the only moment. And the person who has to arrive is the one already standing here.
- [How do I stop needing other people's approval?](https://soulsensis.com/question/how-do-i-stop-needing-approval/): The acceptance and pride I wanted from others were the acceptance and pride I had not yet given myself.
- [How do I let go of pain I keep holding on to?](https://soulsensis.com/question/how-do-i-let-go-of-old-pain/): If it has already given you what it had to give, you are allowed to put it down.
- [Why do I feel stuck in life?](https://soulsensis.com/question/why-do-i-feel-stuck-in-life/): This wanting is what traps you, and forcing change doesn't work. The more you grip to wanting, the further the object of your wanting moves away from you.
- [Why do I wake up with a feeling of dread?](https://soulsensis.com/question/why-do-i-wake-up-with-dread/): This desperate wanting is precisely what is trapping me, as it places excess importance on not being in this depressive state.

## Journal

- [Journal](https://soulsensis.com/journal/): 30 pieces from the author's own journal, as he wrote them.
- [The mind is a tool](https://soulsensis.com/journal/the-mind-is-a-tool/): 25 October 2026. You can feel cold in a dream.
- [A letter to my father](https://soulsensis.com/journal/a-letter-to-my-father/): 16 September 2026. 16 Sep 26
- [A soulful message to those suffering from anxiety and depression](https://soulsensis.com/journal/a-soulful-message-to-those-suffering-from-anxiety-and-depression/): 3 April 2024. For those suffering please know that I am and there are people here for you and the pain you might be experiencing presently is understandable.
- [Why is life so difficult to understand?](https://soulsensis.com/journal/why-is-life-so-difficult-to-understand/): 15 December 2020. I am grappling with the pain of loneliness and the need to develop myself to be able to face life on my own terms and by myself.
- [A man eating a banana](https://soulsensis.com/journal/a-man-eating-a-banana/): 15 December 2020. He seems nonchalant, but also in deep rumination about something.
- [I miss you](https://soulsensis.com/journal/i-miss-you/): 27 November 2020. I miss your smile and the way you somehow infuse joy into every crevice of your lips as you look at me with all the love you could give.
- [Accepting a heartbreak to move on](https://soulsensis.com/journal/accepting-a-heartbreak-to-move-on/): 19 July 2020. Before we met, I always had the assumption that life was tragic, difficult and hard.
- [Losing you: a tribute to heartbreak](https://soulsensis.com/journal/losing-you-a-tribute-to-heartbreak/): 27 June 2020. You'll cry, a lot.
- [I woke up to her crying](https://soulsensis.com/journal/i-woke-up-to-her-crying/): 17 June 2020. It wasn't uncontrolled.
- [Day by day, take it as a win](https://soulsensis.com/journal/day-by-day-take-it-as-a-win/): 29 May 2020. I often ask my friends who are struggling with depression and anxiety: "Are you getting stronger?"
- [I never thought I'd end up with someone like you](https://soulsensis.com/journal/i-never-thought-id-end-up-with-someone-like-you/): 16 May 2020. She was on her phone, snapchatting the coffee I just bought her.
- [I struggle with loneliness](https://soulsensis.com/journal/i-struggle-with-loneliness/): 10 May 2020. Perhaps it takes a true break up, not only romantically, but from social media to truly realise a fatal realisation that I struggle with loneliness.
- [I don't think this is too much to ask for](https://soulsensis.com/journal/i-dont-think-this-is-too-much-to-ask-for/): 28 April 2020. I've been telling myself that I'm doing okay.
- [Akrasia: why do we act against our better judgement?](https://soulsensis.com/journal/akrasia-why-do-we-act-against-our-better-judgement/): 26 April 2020. **Akrasia**: "*the state of mind in which someone acts against their better judgment through weakness of will"*
- [No one can take this away from you](https://soulsensis.com/journal/no-one-can-take-this-away-from-you/): 20 April 2020. Imagine you’re 80, you just smoked a fat joint, you’re kicking back with nothing but your thoughts, your memories, the life that you’ve lived.
- [To the people who helped me through my worst anxiety](https://soulsensis.com/journal/to-the-people-who-helped-me-through-my-worst-anxiety/): 16 April 2020. I went to Malaysia.
- [The hand we're dealt: an honest account of anxiety](https://soulsensis.com/journal/the-hand-were-dealt-an-honest-account-of-anxiety/): 8 April 2020. I never wanted this, a dark cloud which envelops all that is beautiful, a secondary voice telling me to kill myself, a stalker with only eyes for me...
- [Love isn't easy, nor should it be this difficult](https://soulsensis.com/journal/love-isnt-easy-nor-should-it-be-this-difficult/): 5 April 2020. I wept my tears away, struggling to comprehend what was wrong with me.
- [Losing friends after a break-up is hard as hell](https://soulsensis.com/journal/losing-friends-after-a-break-up-is-hard-as-hell/): 28 March 2020. I have to learn how to let go of these people so that I can move on to meeting new people and more importantly, spend time with those that matter...
- [The dread still clings to me like a wet blanket](https://soulsensis.com/journal/the-dread-still-clings-to-me-like-a-wet-blanket/): 22 March 2020. Storytime: The dread and death anxiety still clings to me like a wet blanket, enveloping all that is pure and reminding me who exactly is in charge.
- [The jumper that still smells of her](https://soulsensis.com/journal/the-jumper-that-still-smells-of-her/): 11 February 2020. Storytime: "I brought the jumper towards my face.
- [Anxiety is handed to you, and you live with it](https://soulsensis.com/journal/anxiety-is-handed-to-you-and-you-live-with-it/): 26 January 2020. Anxious thoughts: It's handed to you and you're going to live with it your whole life.
- [Steady recovery](https://soulsensis.com/journal/steady-recovery/): 18 January 2020. I've been getting better, I think… My recovery from my anxiety and depression has forced me to do things which I normally wouldn't do.
- [It's 3:12 am and I'm up writing this](https://soulsensis.com/journal/its-3-12-am-and-im-up-writing-this/): 18 January 2020. I really should fix my sleeping schedule but it's already fucked so can't hurt to fuck it up even more right?
- [Perhaps it's ok to take things slow](https://soulsensis.com/journal/perhaps-its-ok-to-take-things-slow/): 24 December 2019. Diary Entry: Perhaps it’s ok to take things slow.
- [Why is it so hard to do what you say you'll do?](https://soulsensis.com/journal/why-is-it-so-hard-to-do-what-you-say-youll-do/): 23 December 2019. For far too long I feel like I talk the talk but don’t walk the walk – it’s fucked.
- [The intergenerational gap](https://soulsensis.com/journal/the-intergenerational-gap/): 22 December 2019. Note that this piece of writing isn’t perfected (I mean, when has my writing ever been?) and it is on a topic I’ll certainly revisit in the future.
- [The inflated ego of the self-proclaimed influencer](https://soulsensis.com/journal/the-inflated-ego-of-the-self-proclaimed-influencer/): 26 November 2019. I remember being so sucked into this idea cus at the time I had a very inflated ego and just wanted followers.
- [The night I cried in your car](https://soulsensis.com/journal/the-night-i-cried-in-your-car/): 31 October 2019. I'll never forget that night when I cried relentlessly in your car and you were there to comfort me...
- [Do you need anyone else to tell you you're enough?](https://soulsensis.com/journal/do-you-need-anyone-else-to-tell-you-youre-enough/): 28 October 2019. I'm not sure if any of you guys can relate with me here but I've been contemplating a lot lately on the concept of self-validation.
